The Kansas City Current, the NWSL club closely tied to Patrick and Brittany Mahomes, reached a valuation of $275 million, highlighting the rapid growth of womenâs soccer. For Brittany, the moment carried extra meaning because her connection to the Current began years before Patrick officially joined the ownership group.Kansas City Current reaches $275 million valuationIn June 2025, Forbes ranked the Kansas City Current as the second-most valuable club in the National Womenâs Soccer League. The team was valued at $275 million, only slightly behind Angel City FC at $280 million.The Current also led the league in annual revenue, generating roughly $36 million. That figure placed the Kansas City club $1 million ahead of Angel City and offered another sign of how quickly the womenâs soccer market was expanding.The numbers were particularly striking because the Current had only begun playing regular-season matches in 2021. In just a few years, the club had grown from a new NWSL team into one of the leagueâs most valuable franchises.Brittany Mahomes celebrated the milestone on social media by sharing graphics highlighting the Currentâs valuation and league-leading revenue. Her reaction made sense given her personal history with the club.Brittany was one of the founders of the Kansas City womenâs soccer organization in 2020. A former collegiate soccer player at the University of Texas at Tyler, she had a connection to the sport long before the Current became a major business story.Patrick Mahomes later joined the ownership group, adding another high-profile sports figure to the clubâs growing profile.Patrick and Brittany Mahomesâ investment in womenâs soccerPatrick Mahomes has built an expanding sports portfolio beyond his career with the Kansas City Chiefs. His investments have included stakes connected to the Kansas City Royals, Sporting Kansas City and the Alpine Formula 1 team.Still, the Current stands out because of Brittanyâs early involvement. What began as her investment in womenâs soccer eventually became a family connection to a franchise that continued to gain financial momentum.When Patrick announced his ownership stake, he made his excitement clear, writing:âI am thankful for the chance to join @brittanylynne as part of the @thekccurrent ownership team,â Mahomes tweeted when he first purchased ownership stake. âShe and the Longs have done an incredible job building a world-class organization and I am excited to join another championship-caliber club as it continues to make history.âThe Mahomes family has also supported the Current away from the business side, often attending matches with their children. Their presence has helped bring additional attention to a club benefiting from the broader rise of womenâs sports.The $275 million valuation reported last year was therefore more than a financial milestone. It reflected the growing commercial strength of the NWSL and the vision behind the Currentâs rise. articles.title: Travis Kelce makes a major business move with 5% ownership in a product he has relied on for years while expanding his business empire
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce made another major move beyond the football field in January 2026, turning a product he has trusted for years into a business opportunity.
articles.body: Travis Kelce made another major move beyond the football field in January 2026, turning a product he has trusted for years into a business opportunity. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end announced a partnership with Sleep Number Corporation that gave him a 5% ownership stake in the mattress company. For Kelce, the deal is more than another celebrity endorsement. It connects his personal approach to recovery with his growing investment portfolio.Travis Kelceâs Sleep Number investment reflects his focus on recoveryKelceâs decision stands out because Sleep Number is already part of his daily routine. The NFL star said he has used the companyâs bed for years, making the investment a natural extension of an existing relationship rather than a simple promotional deal.His experience as a professional athlete also gives the partnership a clear purpose. Recovery is a major part of an NFL playerâs career, and quality sleep can become increasingly important as the physical demands of football build over time. Sleep Numberâs adjustable beds allow users to change their settings based on their comfort and recovery needs, something Kelce said has mattered throughout his career.Kelce explained his decision in a statement:âa constant through different seasons of my career and life. articles.title: NFL Execs Sound Off on Best International Cities to Host Franchise After Roger Goodell's Comments
articles.summary: London, Mexico City, Toronto and Berlin were mentioned as potential international cities to host NFL teams in light of commissioner Roger Goodell's recent statement that the league will have franchises outside the United States someday.
articles.body:
London, Mexico City, Toronto and Berlin were mentioned as potential international cities to host NFL teams in light of commissioner Roger Goodell's recent statement that the league will have franchises outside the United States someday.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler spoke with NFL team executives and asked them to select cities that would be the best places for the league to have a team if this does come to fruition.

London, per Fowler, was the "overwhelming favorite among league executives."

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

"It's got the facilities, a large economy and the population," an AFC executive told Fowler. "The fanbase there is passionate."

Per Fowler, London hosted 41 NFL games dating back to 1983. London will host three games in October this year, including two featuring the Jacksonville Jaguars on Oct. 11 and 18.

Mexico City and Toronto would certainly assuage any travel concerns about having an international team. Mexico City has hosted five regular season games and will add a sixth on Nov. 22 when the Minnesota Vikings play the San Francisco 49ers. Toronto, of course, is already host to numerous North American professional sports squads.

Berlin just hosted its first NFL game in 2025, when the Indianapolis Colts beat the Atlanta Falcons 31-25 in an overtime thriller. Early returns on that game were good, per an AFC executive to Fowler.

"Great atmosphere," the exec stated. "The (Colts-Falcons) game sold out really quickly, it was loud all game and there was definitely buzz in the city and downtown."

Berlin will also host games in 2027 and 2029, per Fowler.

Goodell made his belief clear that NFL teams will be outside the United States someday during an Aug. 18 interview with Markus Kuhn of RTL/ntv in Germany (h/t Michael David Smith of Pro Football Talk).

"At some point, there will be NFL teams outside the USA," Goodell said. "I have no doubt that this will happen one day."

If so, there are some clear candidates, with London leading the way. In the meantime, the NFL continues its international series with nine regular season games outside the United States. The first-ever regular season game in Australia leads the way, with the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams playing on Thursday, Sept. 10 (Sept. 11 local time) in Melbourne.

articles.title: New 2027 NFL Mock Draft Drops by ESPN Expert, Arch Manning, Dante Moore, More Landing Spots Revealed
articles.summary: Ahead of the start of the 2026 college football and NFL regular seasons, ESPN NFL draft expert Jordan Reid released an early 2027 NFL mock draft on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Ahead of the start of the 2026 college football and NFL regular seasons, ESPN NFL draft expert Jordan Reid released an early 2027 NFL mock draft on Wednesday.

Reid projected quarterbacks to come off the board with each of the first three selections, and his top 10 picks look like this:

1. Cleveland Browns: Dante Moore, QB, Oregon

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

2. Arizona Cardinals: Arch Manning, QB, Texas

3. New York Jets: CJ Carr, QB, Notre Dame

4. Miami Dolphins: Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State

5. Las Vegas Raiders: Cam Coleman, WR, Texas

6. Tennessee Titans: Dylan Stewart, EDGE, South Carolina

7. Carolina Panthers: Leonard Moore, CB, Notre Dame

8. New Orleans Saints: Colin Simmons, EDGE, Texas

9. New York Giants: Will Echoles, DT, Ole Miss

10. Washington Commanders: Charlie Becker, WR, Indiana

Reid included a hypothetical trade in his mock with the Miami Dolphins trading down from No. 1 to No. 4, allowing the Browns to move up and get their much-needed franchise quarterback.

The 2027 draft is shaping up to be a great one in terms of QB talent, and Reid believes Cleveland will go with Oregon's Dante Moore if it gets the opportunity.

Moore surprised many by returning to college rather than entering the 2026 NFL draft, but he now has a chance to firmly establish himself as the top pick in 2027.

In his first full season as a starter, Moore completed 71.8 percent of his passes for 3,565 yards, 30 touchdowns and 10 interceptions, and he figures to get even better in Oregon's high-powered offense.

The Browns' quarterback competition between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders was a mess leading up to head coach Todd Monken naming Watson the starter for 2026, but there is little doubt that the organization would love to avoid a similar situation next year, and selecting Moore would accomplish that goal.

Arizona has a similarly dire quarterback situation led by Jacoby Brissett, so it comes as little surprise that Reid has the Cardinals taking Texas quarterback Arch Manning at No. 2 overall.

While the nephew of legendary NFL quarterbacks Peyton and Eli Manning didn't dominate college football in his first season as a starter in 2025 like many expected, he acquitted himself well and has something to build upon in 2026.

Manning completed 61.4 percent of his passing attempts for 3,163 yards, 26 touchdowns and seven picks, while also rushing for 399 yards and 10 scores last season.

With a year of starting experience under his belt and tons of offensive weaponry around him, everything is lining up for Manning to turn in a huge 2026 campaign ahead of the 2027 draft.

Rounding out the top three picks and the "Big Three" quarterbacks in Reid's mock is Notre Dame's CJ Carr.

As a redshirt freshman in 2025, Carr was highly impressive, completing 66.6 percent of his passes for 2,741 yards, 24 touchdowns and six interceptions.

It has been far too long since the Jets had a true franchise quarterback, and while they have a solid stopgap in Geno Smith for 2026, Carr could finally be the leader and face of the franchise that they have been searching for over the past several years.

As for the Dolphins, trading down from No. 1 to No. 4 in Reid's mock still lands them arguably the best overall player in the draft in Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith.

If the Dolphins trade down, it likely means that quarterback Malik Willis had a solid 2026 season, and getting him a weapon like Smith would only serve to elevate his play even more.

Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix made his preseason debut against the Green Bay Packers last week, marking his first live game action since he broke his ankle in the divisional round of the NFL playoffs in January.

Nix went 6-of-9 passing for 76 yards with one touchdown, leading two scoring drives before watching the rest of the game from the sideline. Denver coach Sean Payton was asked about Nix's return to action after Monday's practice.

"Good. I thought he did a good job," Payton said . "Yes, his movement skills were good. A little fast through one progression, but overall, he did a good job operating the huddle. He's moving around well. [He] had a couple big throws and felt very, very comfortable."

The Green Bay matchup also marked offensive coordinator Davis Webb 's first game calling plays for Nix.

"[It was] smooth, it was good," Payton said of Webb's play-calling. "Communication process was good. Yes, no issues. It was all clean."

The Los Angeles Rams are ready to go whether they have Aaron Donald back on their roster or not. If there was any doubt, Sean McVay has confirmed and made it clear they have plans for if AD is present, and they also have plans for if he's not. No surprise, really, but it's news nonetheless.

The media has been covering the Aaron Donald story throughout the offseason and to be fair, Turf Show Times has done its fair share of work too. Will Donald revise his contract? Does Aaron Donald really want to come back? Would Donald want to the risk the challenge of another NFL season?

So many questions for the Los Angeles Rams and Donald, and Week One against the San Francisco 49ers is fast approaching. There are a lot of takes on whether Donald will be back with the Rams early, later, much later or never. It doesn't seem like anyone with these takes actually knows.

Until anything is confirmed, everyone is waiting for Donald to confirm his plans. If Donald gets to do that on his time and not anyone else's, then know one "knows" what Donald is going to do except Donald. That doesn't stop anyone from speculating, and it can't stop the Rams from preparing.

"We've had plans if he's there, and if he's not," McVay said Tuesday, via the Los Angeles Times.

"Our thought process has been, 'let's look at a 53 with him and a 53 not including him and what does that look like. Whenever a decision is made, if that is the direction he goes where he wants to play, then we have plans accordingly and if not we have plans for those as well."

Contingency plans are common at this time of the season, especially as general managers are confronted with difficult decisions that must be made within the constraints of a 53-man roster. Los Angeles' is unique in that it will have one for the potential return of a franchise legend, but otherwise, it's business as usual."

"Discussing the situation on a recent episode, Mike Florio and his PFT co-host Chris Simms floated a scenario that splits the difference between Donald suiting up Week 1 and staying retired for good: re-signing him and immediately placing him on the physically unable to perform list.

Under that path, Donald would be permitted to work out on his own but couldn't practice with the Rams until the team opens a three-week practice window — at which point he'd get a ramp-up period before any decision on activating him to the 53-man roster."

"If he decides he wants to be able to do it, then the next conversations are: What is your ramp-up ?" McVay said Tuesday, via Benjamin Royer of the ocregister.com. "What does it look like to approach whenever that would be the first time that we think we make the most sense for him to impact and make a positive change with us?

"We've had to have a lot of fluidity and flexibility, and that's what I've had to learn over 10 years. But I think what's good is the thing that has served us well – and it's really the truth – is let's just stay one day at a time."

"Puka Nacua and Myles Garrett have been sidelined from practice for the last two weeks, but they're not the only starters out for the Los Angeles Rams on Tuesday. The Athletic's Nate Atkins noted at the start of practice that Alaric Jackson is absent, and Terrance Ferguson is working off to the side with the training staff like Nacua has been.

It's unclear why Jackson and Ferguson are not practicing; Nacua has a psoas injury, while Garrett is dealing with knee swelling."

That assessment arrives at an ideal time for a Rams team preparing to open the season against the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia.

articles.title: 2026 Fantasy Football Instant Mock Draft, No. 7 Pick: Analysis, key takeaways and full roster
articles.summary: We're onto the No. 7 pick in our Yahoo Instant Mock Draft series for 2026 fantasy football.
articles.body:
As we get ready for the 2026 fantasy football season, there's no better way to prepare than doing mock drafts. And while live mock drafts will give us a great idea of how things might shake out, sometimes they're hit or miss and can be time consuming. Fortunately, Yahoo is offering its Instant Mock Draft tool again this season, available with your Fantasy Plus subscription. If you want to give the tool a spin for free, you can do an Instant Mock Draft for the first three rounds. Head here for more details .

If you're new to the instant mock tool, here are some of the benefits:

Draft immediately : That means no lobbies and no dropouts.

Drafts tailored to your league: No more guessing if a mock draft from a generic 12-team league with standard scoring matches your custom setup. Draft against our algorithm, which mimics your league opponents.

Test strategy: Simulate and try out different draft strategies from your exact draft slot. Find out which approach builds the strongest roster, then nail your live draft with real-time, on-the-clock recommendations.

In this series, I'll be performing an instant mock draft out of each pick slot for 12-team leagues with default half-PPR scoring. Today, we're picking a team from the No. 7 spot. Below is the full roster, plus key takeaways.

No. 1 | No. 2 | No. 3 | No. 4 | No. 5 | No. 6 | No. 7 | No. 8 | No. 9 | No. 10 | No. 11 | No. 12

QB: Caleb Williams, CHI RB: Rhamondre Stevenson, NE RB: Jacory Croskey-Merritt, WAS WR: Amon-Ra St. Brown, DET WR: Nico Collins, HOU TE: George Kittle, SF FLEX: Tee Higgins, CIN Kicker: Tyler Bass, BUF Defense: Patriots Bench: Ladd McConkey, LAC Bench: R.J. Harvey, DEN Bench: Mike Washington Jr., LV Bench: De'Zhaun Stribling, SF Bench: Oronde Gadsden II, LAC Bench: Woody Marks, HOU

I did a mix of thinking like Yahoo analyst Scott Pianowski and a pure Zero RB build. I did a Zero RB look a few mocks ago but it wasn't as drastic as this one; I didn't take my first back until Round 7 with Stevenson here. Normally, I'd be willing to go with three WRs (the max you can start) and then pivot over to RB, but this approach allows you to get solid options at QB and TE so you aren't concerned about streaming much. Let's break down the team a bit.

I was faced with this decision in the first round and opted for the Sun God over the reigning WR champ from a season ago. I think there's plenty that would point to regression for Jaxon Smith-Njigba — Klint Kubiak's departure, Kenneth Walker III leaving, defenses around the NFL adjusting, etc.

One thing Pianowski highlighted are some offenses that have a tight usage tree and make for quality teams to target in fantasy. So we pressed the easy button and went with St. Brown, who has been arguably the most consistent fantasy wideout over the past four seasons. In that stretch, he hasn't finished outside the top 10 at his position and was top-five three times, plus top-15 overall in fantasy in two of those campaigns. There's so much working in Detroit's favor, from the coaching staff to Jared Goff at QB to playing most games indoors. Having the chance to take a player like St. Brown in this range is why Joel Smyth has the No. 7 slot ranked fourth if you can choose your own first-round pick in 2026.

Collins, Higgins and McConkey round out the WR room. The Texans lost Jayden Higgins, and while Collins was always going to be a target hog, that sentiment got a boost. Higgins is on another one of those destination teams for Pianowski in the Bengals with very little usage competition outside him, Ja'Marr Chase and Chase Brown. McConkey is a Year 3 breakout candidate and should bounce back with the Chargers' O-line in better health.

There were a few QBs on the board alongside Williams — Dak Prescott and Justin Herbert to name a few. It felt like a reach on Dak, whom I think has a capped ceiling and some age concerns. Herbert would have made an OK stack with McConkey but I also have him as my WR4, so I wouldn't want to force myself into pairing Herbert and McConkey week-to-week. Williams was quietly the QB5 in overall fantasy scoring in 2025 and while I hate to admit it as a Packers fan, he should only improve with another year under Ben Johnson. Plus, all those weapons — Rome Odunze, Colston Loveland, Luther Burden III, D'Andre Swift. I also think Williams has some untapped, sneaky Aaron Rodgers-esque rushing upside this season.

Kittle got an encouraging report on his recovery from an Achilles tear and appears on track to not start the season on the PUP list. Now, this doesn't mean he will play Week 1. The 49ers could hold him out for a bit. But I feel fine rolling out secondary options or a TE streaming (Jake Tonges) early in the season until Kittle gets up to speed. Kittle's ADP is rising and I did reach on him a bit, but even in this range he has a great chance of returning value as someone who was the TE3 in FPPG last season. San Fran would be one injury to Mike Evans away from Kittle being the clear top receiving option on the offense. He'd be a red-zone target hog and give me a great floor/ceiling combo with this build.

There are plenty of solid late-round RB options that come a bit after the RB Dead Zone . I also wanted to grab a few RBs who have receiving chops, elevating their floor for PPR formats. JCM as my RB2 gives me some worry, though his ADP has been on the rise lately . He's also a favorite sleeper of Justin Boone's for a reason . We now know TreVeyon Henderson is at least a little banged up, though he should be fine. Still, Stevenson was already ahead of him on the depth chart, it's a top offense in New England and he can catch passes.

Harvey and Marks feel like two second-year backs who are being grossly overlooked. Are we really expecting an oft-injured J.K. Dobbins or a rookie to be ahead of Harvey in Denver? Sure, there are between-the-tackles concerns but we know for sure Harvey will be involved in what should be a solid passing attack. Same for Marks. David Montgomery has a lot of miles and should see plenty of goal-line work. But the coaching staff may want to keep Monty fresh and Marks should be in there in passing situations at least. As players available well outside the top 100 picks, you could do worse than Harvey and Marks as your backup RBs in fantasy.

Oh yeah, and we almost forgot about rising star Mike Washington Jr. In a Zero RB build, I want to target players with a path to RB1 status. Even if Ashton Jeanty misses a week or two, great, Washington is probably an RB1 in those weeks. If this injury lingers at all, Washington likely has RB2/3 upside, plus we know he'll be involved even when Jeanty is healthy, given Kubiak's play-calling.

Zero RB isn't for the faint of heart. You need to be very prepared with RB targets late in the draft and feel confident in those picks, otherwise you're going to leave the draft feeling a bit panicked. Also, keep in mind that you have WR depth for a reason. We know we only have three spots for WRs and if all four are performing at a high level (and someone on the bench emerges), we can trade that depth for RB help. I'd classify this strategy as a bit more advanced, so be sure to read up on all our free content here in the Draft Kit .

articles.title: Before you go RB-RB to start your fantasy draft, consider this warning
articles.summary: Something happened last season that hasn't happen since 2011 or earlier. It's a statistical outlier disguised as a new norm.
articles.body:
Something happened last season that hasn't happened since 2011 or earlier. It's a statistical outlier disguised as a new norm. If you're planning to take two running backs in the first two rounds of your fantasy draft, consider the following.

The top-10 RBs -- based on ADP -- entering Week 1 last year collectively missed only four games all season, accounting for only 2% of their teams' contests. How unusual was that? Across the previous 14 seasons, dating back to 2012, the top-10 ADP running backs had missed an average of 19% of their games.

What happened in 2011 or earlier? No clue, because reliable ADPs are hard to find prior to 2012. So, for all intents and purposes, last year's top-10 RBs were durable to an unprecedented degree.

As a result, most of them crushed it fantasy-wise; that's what happens when great starters stay on the field week after week. Also, as a result, most of them are once again in the top 10 in ADP.

Not surprising, and also quite concerning, especially considering Christian McCaffrey's massive injury/regression risks , Saquon Barkley's advancing age and high-end handcuff status, and Jonathan Taylor's extensive injury history, which most managers seem to have forgotten after last year's MVP-level output.

To be clear, some RBs are safer than others. But collectively, what happened last year was an anomaly. We should expect this year's top 10 to miss at least 15% of their games. Hopefully you pick the right guys.

For a deeper dive into the overall risks of going RB-RB in your draft, listen to this recent podcast episode .

A deal with the NFL, critics say, puts the credibility of that entire probe in serious doubt.Why is The Athletic being called hypocritical over the Dianna Russini-Mike Vrabel investigation?The criticism isn't coming from anonymous corners of the internet. OutKick columnist Armando Salguero wrote directly about the contradiction at the heart of The Athletic's situation, and his words cut straight to the point."The Athletic is presumably in the throes of this conflict of interest investigation of a former reporter with an NFL coach while at the same time engaging in talks to enter into a conflict of interest situation with the NFL. Got it," Salguero wrote.He didn't stop there. "That raises a sizeable inconsistency. The Athletic is presumably investigating Russini for possibly engaging in a questionable relationship with an NFL coach at a time it is weighing whether to get in bed with the NFL."The argument isn't complicated. The Athletic has strict editorial guidelines that govern its staff, and those guidelines were central to why the Russini probe was launched in the first place. An institutional partnership with the NFL would place the outlet in essentially the same position it is investigating Russini for. Salguero made that parallel explicit: "So will The Athletic, on the one hand trying to avoid the appearance of a conflict of interest, allow an affiliation with the NFL that violates its own guidelines by calling into question its credibility?"That's not a rhetorical flourish. It's a real question with real consequences for how seriously anyone should take the outcome of this investigation.What happens to the Dianna Russini investigation if The Athletic partners with the NFL?That's where things get genuinely murky. Others have already questioned whether The Athletic will even release the findings of the Russini investigation if the NFL partnership is finalized. The incentive to publish a critical report about a league you're now financially aligned with is, to put it plainly, not great.The scandal itself began when Russini and Vrabel were photographed together at a resort in Arizona, appearing to hug, hold hands, and lounge by the pool. It turned into a months-long tabloid story, with fans combing through old interviews, social media posts, and even Spotify playlists for more context. Russini resigned from The Athletic, and Vrabel stepped away from his Patriots duties on Day 3 of the 2026 NFL Draft to attend counseling with his family.Since then, both have largely gone quiet. Vrabel has appeared at press conferences. Russini has not addressed the situation publicly beyond her initial statement and resignation letter. She deleted her social media accounts and recently referred to herself as a "former journalist" in text messages that leaked to a New York Times reporter, suggesting she isn't planning a return to sports media.The investigation, meanwhile, sits in an uncomfortable place. An outlet probing editorial bias while negotiating closer ties to the very organization at the center of that bias story isn't exactly a clean look. Whether The Athletic acknowledges that tension publicly or quietly lets the partnership reshape what the probe produces, the outcome either way is going to draw scrutiny.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Texas quarterback Arch Manning ranks third and Oregon signal-caller Dante Moore sits sixth on the latest 2027 NFL draft big board from Dane Brugler of The Athletic, who listed his first 50 players.
articles.body:
Texas quarterback Arch Manning ranks third and Oregon signal-caller Dante Moore sits sixth on the latest 2027 NFL draft big board from Dane Brugler of The Athletic, who listed his first 50 players.

Here's a look at the top 10, which begins with Ohio State superstar wide receiver Jeremiah Smith.

Five other quarterbacks are on the list: Notre Dame's CJ Carr (No. 27), Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker (No. 30), Ole Miss' Trinidad Chambliss (No. 35), South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers (No. 37) and Miami's Darian Mensah (No. 41).

The 6'4", 230-pound Manning is entering his second season as Texas' starter. Last year, he completed 61.4 percent of his passes for 3,163 yards (7.8 YPA), 26 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He also rushed for 399 yards and 10 scores.

Texas has great expectations this year, as it did last year, when the team started the season No. 1 in the preseason poll. The Longhorns went 10-3 and missed the College Football Playoff, but they are fifth in this year's preseason poll.

Here's what Brugler had to say about Mannning.

"Manning is not without flaws. However, his issues are mostly experience based, and his progress last season will encourage evaluators that continued growth is coming. Better timing with his receivers and upgrades to the depth chart (hello, Cam Coleman) also should translate to better play," Brugler wrote.

"Drafting a quarterback high in the NFL Draft is a substantial bet, without guarantees. But based on the promise of his tape and traits, Manning looks like the type of prospect worth the gamble. We'll see if his 2026 tape builds on that optimism."

Moore transferred from Oregon after starring at UCLA in 2023. He got the QB1 job in 2025, completing 71.8 percent of his passes for 3,565 yards (8.7 YPA), 30 touchdowns and 10 picks. The Ducks went 13-2 last year and reached the College Football Playoff semifinal.

Moore could have very well been a high draft pick in 2025, but he decided to return for another year. Brugler wrote the following in part:

"Had he declared, Moore would have been drafted very high in the 2026 NFL Draft — likely No. 2 by the New York Jets. However, he wanted one more year of college experience to continue developing mentally and physically."

Oregon has high expectations again, slotting second in the AP preseason poll.

We'll see how the draft board adjusts as the season goes along, but it's clear Manning and Moore lead the way to start on the QB list.
